I am Dr. Hephzibah Rani Singh from India, with a doctorate and a passion for science education and innovation. We are developing an intelligent lunar mission planning application that helps users compare potential moon landing locations and identify suitable mission dates. The application is based on three factors:

1. Terrain Suitability 2. Sunlight Availability 3. Earth Visibility 4. Mission Suitability

Looking for: Python/data analysts (NASA datasets), UI/UX Experts, earth science experts.
summary:
Catherine Lunar Navigator (LUNA-OPT) is an educational lunar mission planning and landing-site analysis application developed using Python and Streamlit. It helps explore potential lunar landing regions by combining NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data with terrain analysis, estimated sunlight availability, and Earth-visibility calculations.

The application evaluates candidate locations using indicators such as average elevation, surface slope, and terrain roughness. A mission scoring engine ranks the candidate sites, while a rule-based Mission Advisor highlights positive indicators and areas requiring further investigation. An interactive dashboard presents mission suitability scores, comparative charts, terrain measurements, and downloadable reports.

LUNA-OPT aims to make lunar exploration data easier to understand and demonstrate how scientific datasets and computational tools can support preliminary landing-site assessment. It is an educational research prototype, and its results are preliminary indicators rather than certified landing-safety assessments.
details:
Project Details – Catherine Lunar Navigator (LUNA-OPT)

LUNA-OPT (Lunar Exploration and Landing-Site Intelligence) is an interactive educational prototype designed to help explore and compare potential lunar landing regions using terrain and environmental indicators.

The application analyses candidate lunar locations using NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation dataset. It evaluates terrain characteristics such as average elevation, surface slope and roughness to estimate preliminary terrain suitability. It also includes simplified models to estimate sunlight availability and Earth visibility, which are important considerations for lunar mission planning.

The system combines these indicators through a mission-scoring engine to rank candidate locations and provide a rule-based Mission Advisor. Users can explore the results through an interactive dashboard featuring comparison charts, technical workspaces and downloadable mission reports.

Technology Used: Python, Streamlit, NumPy, Pandas, Rasterio and Plotly. The application uses NASA LOLA lunar elevation data for terrain analysis.

Creativity and Innovation: LUNA-OPT integrates multiple lunar site assessment indicators into one interactive platform. Its visual dashboard makes complex scientific information easier for students and beginners to understand and explore.

Benefits and Intended Impact: The project promotes space science education, practical programming skills and awareness of lunar exploration challenges. It demonstrates how publicly available NASA datasets and open-source technologies can be used to develop useful educational research tools.

LUNA-OPT is an independent educational and research prototype. Its candidate coordinates and simplified environmental models are illustrative, and its results are preliminary indicators rather than certified landing-site safety assessments.
